title: Quick check: CSS Fundamentals for React

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “CSS Fundamentals for React”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Selectors and the cascade should support responsive layouts, visible focus, and maintainable component styling.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Selectors and the cascade should support responsive layouts, visible focus, and maintainable component styling.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS Fundamentals for React: Selectors and the cascade should support responsive layouts, visible focus, and maintainable component styling.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Selectors and the cascade?
options: Prefer semantic HTML, consistent design tokens, responsive rules, and reduced-motion support.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Prefer semantic HTML, consistent design tokens, responsive rules, and reduced-motion support.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS Fundamentals for React: Prefer semantic HTML, consistent design tokens, responsive rules, and reduced-motion support.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “CSS Fundamentals for React” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in CSS Fundamentals for React: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
